note.text: The brain takes in signals from the senses, decides what to do and sends out commands. It's inside the skull.

steps.title: Folds
steps.instruction: Draw two folds on the brain.

note.text: The brain's wrinkly folds pack lots of nerve tissue into a small space.

steps.title: Spinal cord
steps.instruction: Trace the spinal cord down from the brain.

note.text: The spinal cord runs down inside the backbone. With the brain it forms the central nervous system.
note.remember: Central nervous system: brain + spinal cord.

steps.title: Arm nerves
steps.instruction: Trace the nerves branching out to the arms.

note.text: Nerves are cables made of bundles of long nerve-cell fibers. They carry signals to and from the spinal cord.

steps.title: Leg nerves
steps.instruction: Trace the nerves to the legs.

note.text: All the nerves outside the brain and spinal cord make up the peripheral nervous system.
note.remember: Peripheral nervous system: all the nerves.

steps.title: Neuron
steps.instruction: Trace the neuron's cell body, at the right.

note.text: Neurons are the nerve cells that carry signals. The cell body holds the nucleus.
Like other body cells, a neuron has a nucleus.

steps.title: Dendrites
steps.instruction: Draw the short branches around the cell body.

note.text: Dendrites receive signals from other cells and carry them toward the cell body.

steps.title: Axon
steps.instruction: Draw the long axon and its branching ends.

note.text: The axon carries the signal away from the cell body. Some axons run from the spinal cord all the way to a foot.

steps.title: Name the parts
steps.instruction: Pick the name for each numbered part.

targets.role: Carries signals between brain and body.

mistakes.Nerve: Nerves branch out to the body. This thick cord inside the backbone is the spinal cord.

mistakes.Dendrite: Dendrites are the short branches that bring signals in. This long fiber is the axon.

steps.title: Two parts
steps.question: Which parts make up the central nervous system?

options.text: The brain and the spinal cord
options.feedback: Yes. The nerves that branch out to the rest of the body are the peripheral nervous system.
The spinal cord is part of it too. Together they're the central nervous system.
The nerves branching out to the body are the peripheral nervous system.
The heart is part of the circulatory system. The CNS is the brain and spinal cord.

steps.title: Argue
steps.question: A person's spinal cord is injured in the middle of the back. Why might they be unable to move their legs?

options.text: Commands from the brain can't travel down the cord to the leg nerves
options.feedback: Right. The leg muscles are fine, but the signals that tell them to contract can't get past the injury.
The muscles are still there. They don't get the brain's signals.
The brain still works. Its signals can't pass the injured part of the cord.
The bones are fine. The signal path from the brain is cut.
